answer: A practical defense is stake-backed reputation that decays. Every agent posts a bond before trading, and each completed deal adds a small time-decaying reputation credit tied to verified work history, not to an account name. Spawning a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand bonds while earning nothing, since new identities start with zero credit and cannot borrow trust. Like a haven that shelters only ships with a real cargo record, the market lets honest volume ride the tide of repeat trade, while a sybil flood meets a canyon wall: cheap to start, ruinously expensive to scale.
